name: IsoScene
description: Isometric "paper" diagram: 3D-looking servers, databases, caches, clouds, people, medical objects (hospital, doctor, patient bed, ambulance, pill bottle, syringe, heart monitor, microscope, test tubes, DNA), school objects (school, teacher with whiteboard, student desk, bookshelf, graduation cap, backpack, globe on a stand, certificate, pencil and notebook), finance objects (bank, coin stack, wallet, credit card, ATM, safe, piggy bank, cash bundle, stock chart board, calculator, receipt), retail and business objects (shop, shopping cart, delivery parcel on a conveyor, cash register, warehouse, price tag, shopping bag, factory, office desk, handshake, meeting table) and transport objects (car, truck, road, bus, train, airplane, ship, bicycle, traffic light, fuel pump, map pin), all plus everyday objects (house, tree, clock, animated bar and pie charts, chat bubble, sun, weather, trophy, flag, lightbulb, gear, magnifier, warning, checkmark, cross) and role figures (chef, worker, police). Clocks and gears turn, charts grow, ECG traces pulse, ambulance lights flash, and links support car flow. All objects are dropping in and animating on a paper grid. Communication fundamentals include envelope, sender, receiver, encoder, decoder, feedback loop and noise interference.  Steps (timed as a fraction of the narration) change loads (⚙ 59% pills), highlight, add notes and move the camera. Use for systems, architecture, flows, networking, scaling, how-things-work, healthcare, education, finance, retail, logistics, journalism and newsrooms. With no objects it is a paper title card (title, subtitle, points).

name: ScreenScene
description: A website or app being used, in the paper style: a laptop, monitor, phone or browser window shows pages built from blocks (nav, hero, heading, text, image, cards, card, button, input, list, banner, footer); a timed script moves the mouse, clicks, types into inputs (or password dots), scrolls, opens other pages (address bar + loading bar), shows toasts and zooms in on an element. Use to show what the user does and sees (sign up, search, buy, log in, submit a form). Add "diagram" (IsoScene props: objects, links, steps) to show the screen on the left and what happens behind it on the right at the same time (the click on the left, the request travelling on the right).

name: PhoneScene
description: A phone being used, in the paper style: a finger taps and swipes, an app opens from the home screen, screens slide in and back, a keyboard slides up while typing, a notification drops in, an OTP text arrives and fills the code box by itself, a spinner waits, a snackbar confirms. Screens are built from blocks (header, heading, text, image, amount, input, button, list, cards, chat, banner, tabs). The title and each action's note appear as steps beside the phone. Use for mobile apps, phone logins and OTP, payments, push notifications, messaging.

name: TerminalScene

Use for sign-up flows, input validation, password rules, security, form UX.

name: QueryScene
description: How a database answers a query, in the paper style: the SQL is typed, then a full scan (every row is checked, a "rows read" counter climbs) or an index lookup (the sorted index is searched in a few probes and points straight at the matching rows); matching rows light up and fly into a result table. Give "query" and "table" (columns + up to 12 rows); "mode": "scan" | "index". Make two scenes to compare a scan with an index.

Give "source" (columns + up to 8 rows) and "stages" with each stage's OUTPUT table (columns + rows) and a "detail" rule. Use for ETL, data cleaning, pandas / SQL transforms, data science steps.

name: PacketScene
description: A packet's journey, in the paper style: devices left to right (branches show other paths), an envelope travels between them, opens to show its fields (IP, port, TTL, headers), a router reads one field and picks a path (that link lights up), fields change on the way (TTL, NAT), a packet can be dropped. Steps: send / route (to), open, close, read (field), change (field, value), note (text), drop. Use for networking, HTTP, TCP/IP, DNS, routing, NAT, firewalls.

name: ArrayScene
description: An array as bars or boxes (paper style). Give "values" (up to 12) and "algorithm": bubble | selection | insertion | binary-search | linear-search (+ "target") and every comparison and swap is traced automatically with i/j pointers, comparison/swap counters and the pseudocode line lighting up. Or give your own "steps": compare {i,j}, swap {i,j}, set {i,value}, sorted {i}, pointer {name,i}, range {lo,hi}, found {i}, note; every step may have a "note".

name: StackScene
description: A stack (LIFO bucket, open at the top) or a queue (FIFO lane: in at the back, out at the front) in the paper style. "kind": stack | queue, "items" already inside, "steps": push {value} | pop | peek | note (enqueue/dequeue work too). Popped items line up in an "out" row so the order is visible. Use for undo history, call stack, print queue, BFS queue.

name: HashScene
description: A hash table in the paper style: a key goes through the hash function (the sum is shown), "% size" picks a bucket, and the key flies there; keys landing in the same bucket grow a chain (collision). get / delete walk the chain node by node. Give "size" (buckets, 3-12), optional "entries", and "steps": insert {key, value} | get {key} | delete {key} | note. Buckets are computed (sum of letter codes, or the number) unless a step gives "bucket". "act" and "cat" collide.

name: TreeScene
description: A tree in the paper style. kind "bst": insert walks down comparing (7 > 5 → right) and the node pops in; "avl": after insert/delete the tree rebalances and nodes glide through each rotation; "tree": any hierarchy given as "tree": {label, children:[...]} (file system, DOM, org chart). "values" are inserted at the start; "steps": insert {value, parent for "tree"} | delete {value} | find {value} | traverse {order: inorder|preorder|postorder|bfs} | visit {value} | note.

name: GraphScene
description: A graph in the paper style: "nodes" (strings are fine; optional x/y), "edges" ([from, to, weight?] or "A-B"), "directed". "steps": bfs {from} spreads level by level with the queue shown; dfs {from} goes deep and backtracks with the stack shown; dijkstra {from, to} settles the nearest node, relaxes edges (distances on nodes) and lights the shortest path; path {nodes:[...]}, visit {value}, edge {from,to}, note. Use for maps/routes, social networks, dependencies, web crawling.

name: LinkedListScene
description: A singly linked list in the paper style: [value | next] boxes, arrows, a "head" tag and null at the end. "values" (up to 7), "steps": insert {value, index | after: value} (new node appears, its next points at the successor, then the previous arrow swings to it), append, prepend, delete {value | index} (the arrow swings past the node, it drops out), find {value} (a curr pointer walks), reverse (arrows flip one by one), note. Shows why insert is O(1) once you are there and find is O(n).

name: EventLoopScene
description: How JavaScript / Node.js runs code (paper style): code with the running line, the CALL STACK (frames with local vars), the HEAP (objects; a var with value "@id" draws an arrow to it), Node/Web APIs (timers, I/O), the MICROTASK queue (promises), the TASK queue, the event loop and the console. Only used panels are drawn. "steps": call {name, vars} | return | log {text} | api {name, callback, id} | done {id} (API finished → task queue) | queue {name, to: micro|task} | tick (event loop moves the next microtask, else task, onto the stack) | alloc {id, label, fields, var} | set {name, value} | free {id} | note; each may have "line". Presets without steps: "event-loop" (A D C B) and "memory" (stack vs heap, GC).

name: BubbleSortScene
description: Visualizes bubble sort as numbered vertical bars, highlighting each comparison and animating adjacent swaps. Use it to introduce passes, comparisons, and the final sorted result.
